intent: Hold the application shell's sidebar state (expanded or collapsed on desktop, open or closed on mobile) and lay the sidebar and the main area out side by side.
typical_uses: The outermost element of an application shell with a persistent side navigation panel

dont_use_when.situation: A panel that opens for one task and is dismissed afterwards (filters, a form, item details)
A panel that slides in from an edge for one task and is dragged or swiped away

invariants.text: `open` and `defaultOpen` are both accepted; `defaultOpen` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `open` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

Every desktop expand or collapse writes the `sidebar_state` cookie (path `/`, seven days), controlled or not. With `defaultOpen` omitted the provider renders expanded first and restores the cookie's value after mount; with `defaultOpen` given, the cookie is not read.
Cmd+B or Ctrl+B pressed anywhere in the window toggles the sidebar (the event's default is prevented), the same call SidebarTrigger and SidebarRail make.
Below a 768px viewport a toggle opens or closes the mobile sheet instead of changing `open`, so `onOpenChange` is not called for it.
The provider wraps its subtree in a TooltipProvider with `delay` 0, so every Tooltip inside it opens with no wait unless a nearer TooltipProvider sets its own `delay`.

The panel widths are the `--sidebar-width` (16rem) and `--sidebar-width-icon` (3rem) custom properties set on the provider's element; a `style` entry for either one overrides it for every part inside. The mobile sheet is fixed at 18rem and ignores both.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Pair `open` with `onOpenChange` and write the next value back, or drop both and use `defaultOpen` - a controlled provider never moves on its own, so the trigger, the rail and the shortcut appear to do nothing

anti_patterns.dont: Read or write the `sidebar_state` cookie directly
anti_patterns.do_instead: Observe and drive the state through `open` and `onOpenChange`; the cookie write is internal to the provider

onOpenChange.states: onOpenChange is a function called with the next desktop open value, not a value
onOpenChange.because: A function type has no JSON Schema representation. It fires on every desktop toggle whether or not `open` is controlled, and never for the mobile sheet.

good.title: Sidebar and main area as siblings under the provider

bad.title: The main area nested inside the panel
bad.why: SidebarInset is the panel's sibling, not its content: inside Sidebar it renders in the fixed panel, collapses with it and moves into the mobile sheet.

companions.typed_by: () => { state: 'expanded' | 'collapsed'; open: boolean; setOpen: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>; openMobile: boolean; setOpenMobile: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>; isMobile: boolean; toggleSidebar: () => void }
companions.description: Reads the nearest SidebarProvider's state and controls, for a custom trigger or for UI elsewhere in the shell that follows the sidebar. Throws when called outside a SidebarProvider.

cannot_extract: default: prop "defaultOpen" is read through `??` and also as its own value, so no one literal is its default - the contract states no default for it

onOpenChange.description: Partially typed: ((open: boolean) => void) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property and none for this one; shape checked by tsc, see x-uikit.partially_typed_props. onOpenChange is a function called with the next desktop open value, not a value.
